notes.title: The Hunt Concludes
notes.notes:
[h3]Dear acolytes,[/h3]

Since March 25, 2024, we have had the pleasure of designing, developing, and sharing content for Acolyte of the Altar with all of you. Thank you for your continued support and consistent feedback as we all fought our way through the Marrow Wastes, Fading Forest, and Red Shores.

What started as one person's daydream became a seven-person team creating our debut game. We have learned so much from this experience. Both in creating a game for one of our favorite genres, and in growing a community that wanted to be a part of the process, this has been a journey that we will forever be grateful for. Because of your support, we spent the past year making Acolyte of the Altar bigger and better than we could've ever done on our own.

[b]Finishing our first game is bittersweet.[/b] We'd love to spend more time in the wastes together, but we're proud of our creation and how much it has developed. The time we’ve regained will be put to great use on our next game, a new and exciting adventure we’ll say more about when the time is right. Follow along, as you do not want to miss it!

[h3]Thanks to all of you players, here’s a summary of everything we’ve added to Acolyte of the Altar after launch.[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/ca3887a884aae90b9ef73ef5d243243d2c92df2c.png[/img]

The most substantial improvement has been the addition of 74 all-new Fabled variants of cards that you can unlock by having the base version of a card in your deck when you complete a run, doubling the former card count at launch. These were an absolute blast to design and to play around with when developing, and it was super rewarding to see the community’s reactions live while releasing them in a three-wave structure! We live-streamed developer commentary of us playing with the new cards after they were all released, talking about different details of their inspiration.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/f33ed2c938a67ffcd236b1216e6946032b979eb4.png[/img]

The most recent addition of new Events has increased the variety in the choices available when traversing through the wasteland. More specifically, we’ve added seven Events, more than doubling the initial pool that was available at launch! These include events with unpredictable outcomes and ones that have Patron-specific choices.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/5b0ddfa19da70ed4afc3a2ec0bfc2bf4becacc67.png[/img]

We’ve added five new Gifts to the roster that can be offered as rewards in runs after completing certain objectives. One can be found after defeating each of the three final Bosses, one can be found after unlocking all of the Bestiary entries, and one can be found after unlocking all of the Fabled variants in the Card Library.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/12fc202404bd01b0bfd760e4e78b9c04c1825333.gif[/img]

In addition to improving the reliability of unlocking Achievements in general, we’ve added two new Achievements for the most dedicated of Acolytes to unlock.

After testing and analyzing the play patterns that differentiate the strategies of the Patrons and styles of the Monsters, we’ve balanced many of the cards, beast encounters, and gifts according to our intended experience. The most evident balance changes include updating the Hydrozoan Hivemind fight to offer a more strategic choice between damaging the Monster or damaging its jellyfish friends and reworking the Crumbling City’s Excavate ability to add to its Remaining Residents in order to improve that encounter’s cohesion, though there are many more minute ones that are no less important. For more specific notes, browse the News section of the Steam page or the #patch-notes channel of our Discord server.

This summary wouldn’t be complete without a mention of all of the quality of life improvements and bug fixes that have been included in the patches throughout the year. These include (but are not limited to) adding support for Cloud Saves, expanding the Bestiary to include lore for final Bosses, adding Filters to the Card Library, and improving the readability and accessibility in many of the screens in the game. We wouldn’t have been able to iron out many of the bugs without our dedicated community members reporting bugs in our Discord server!

[b]If you want to stay connected with us, we are active on all our social media accounts! This game is very special to us, and we hope you enjoyed your hunt.
[/b]
[h3]Thank you again, acolytes. And, of course, may the Patrons bless you all.

- Cameron, Lionel, Kennedy, James, Donald, Nico, and Alex
The Black Kite Games Team
[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/1dde982bfa69b82136762ba311b68963070b559f.png[/img]

notes.title: January 2025 Update
notes.notes:
Happy New Year Acolytes!

This update introduces additional visual style and bug fixes. Hope you enjoy!

[h2]Patch Notes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added Charge to Awakening Bear.
[*] Added an animation that plays when entering the Time Portal.
[*] Fixed a bug that inadvertently caused a monster’s Bite ability to deal more than 2 damage at the start of an encounter.
[*] Fixed an error that prevented some cards from being improved or weakened in events.

[*] Fixed some grammatical and spelling errors.

notes.title: December 2024 Update
notes.notes:
We've got an [i]eventful[/i] update for you today! That's right, we've added more [b]Events[/b] that you can encounter in the wastelands!

Thank you for playing and supporting Acolyte of the Altar. We hope you enjoy the new content and wish you and yours happy holidays and a fantastic new year!

[h2]Full Patch Notes[/h2]
[h3]Additions[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added seven (7) new Events to encounter! Vary your runs even more with new choices to make, including some Events that have unpredictable outcomes, Events that have Patron-specific choices, and more…

[/list]
[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Loaine’s Tooth now doubles Shuddering Bundle’s Play ability correctly.

notes.title: November 2024 Update
notes.notes:
Greetings Acolytes! The latest update introduces new content in the form of additional Gifts that can be found after completing certain objectives (as listed in the full patch notes below).

Additionally, we’ve addressed issues that some folks have been having that involve failing to unlock Achievements. In addition to adding two completely new Achievements, now the unlocking of Achievements should be more reliable in general, and most of them can be unlocked retroactively when you open the game.

[h2]Full Patch Notes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added five all-new Gifts! One for each of the final Bosses, one that can be found after unlocking all of the Cards in the library, and one that can be found after unlocking all of the Bestiary entries.
[*] Added two new Steam Achievements and improved the reliability of unlocking all of the achievements in general.
[*] Changed Fungal Explosive to Explosive Chain, which reads “Deal 4 damage. Next turn, deal 8 damage. The turn after, deal 12 damage, then the following turn deal 16 damage.”
[*] Changed Awakening Bear to a (4) mana 2/2 with Fearless and “If you’ve attacked this turn, I cost 1 less.”
[*] Changed Tacklewire’s text to “Start of Turn: I move as close as I can to the center of your board, then I give adjacent allies +1/+1.”
[*] Changed Goat with the Man’s Body’s text to clarify that the discover effects you choose do count as spells you play (for Giant Lantern, for example).
[*] Fixed a bug that allowed you to play Infected Nomad on a full board when its Dominate cost had been reduced to 0.
[*] Fixed a bug that caused the Arcana ability of a monster to change inadvertently after returning to the main menu.
[/list]

notes.title: Fabled Cards Wave II
notes.notes:
Hello Acolytes! We are excited to release the second wave of Fabled card variants.

Additionally, this update comes with a bevy of improvements and changes intended to make your journey through the wasteland better!

Massive shout-out and thanks to the Acolytes who report bugs in our [url=https://discord.gg/gA59RDpG]Discord server[/url]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/173f6bf9e5d4f25fe9cd47ce438b0a5d1664f08b.png[/img]

[h2]Full Change Log[/h2]
[h3]Additions[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added 24 additional Fabled cards that can be unlocked by completing runs with them in your deck.
[*] Added all-new flavor text to all Fabled cards!
[*] Show an “Are You Sure?” panel before deleting progression data.
[*] Added a Keyword Glossary to browse the mechanics on cards in the game, accessible from the main menu.
[*] Updated the notification icon that appears when a card variant is unlockable.
[*] Added a visual indicator of your spiritual burden when in events so as to make decision-making easier.
[*] See a list of your gifts when in events and when looting cards in order to view potential synergies more easily.
[/list]
[h3]Buffs[/h3]
[list]
[*] Changed Enduring Dactyl’s damage-dealing ability from 20 to 25% of enemy’s maximum health. A percentage-based approach to this damage output as a benefit for reaching its condition will help make this ability feel more rewarding, especially against beasts with larger life totals.
[*] Added Overkill back to the Yearning Woods’ Hanger Tantrum. (It was removed before.)
[/list]
[h3]Nerfs[/h3]
[list]
[*] Changed Perinthia, Black Death's first ability from “Play: Infest three enemy abilities” to “Play: Infest two enemy abilities”. We felt like Perinthia was able to generate just a little too much value for its mana cost, so this change reflects a desire to bring her more back in line with the intended infest experience.
[*] Changed Dialect of the Deep from “Discard a card. Gain mana equal to its cost until end of turn. Draw a card.” to “Discard a card. Refill mana equal to its cost. Draw a card.” This limits the amount of mana you can gain to your current maximum mana value. This ramping card could be extorted too easily, leading to decks that capitalized on many creatures with large mana costs that ended battles too fast, so this change will limit the speed at which this deck archetype can get overly effective.
[/list]
[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug that caused monster ability intents to be invisible sometimes.
[*] Gilded Grifter no longer unexpectedly copies cards.
[*] Fixed a bug that overrode the selected choice for skipping the intro and credits in the options.
[*] Fixed a softlock that happened occasionally in the King of Beggars fight.
[*] Fixed a bug that allowed players to attack multiple times in one turn incorrectly.
[*] Fixed a bug that prevented Counterattacks from triggering after Rallying.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes for Hotfix - August 13, 2024
notes.notes:

notes.title: June 3 Balance Update Patch Notes
notes.notes:
Greetings Acolytes!

We are proud to announce a balance patch including changes that we have been working on as part of our roadmap towards more robust improvements to the card pool and the general quality of life of the game experience.

The most substantial improvements are geared toward increasing the playability of some things we felt were unfairly neglected, including Pass Down The Crown, Brain Drinker, and Tiny Hoof. Additionally, encounters against Beasts such as Hydrozoan Hivemind and The Crumbling City have been revamped in order to increase the strategic options available at the player's disposal and to achieve more equitable chances of success for a wider variety of deck archetypes.

Here are some of the more noticeable changes included in the patch, although there are more minor bug fixes and general improvements not mentioned below.

Buffs
• Afflicted Nomad’s triggered ability now deals damage whenever an enemy ability is Ignited in addition to whenever one is Infested.
• Made Pass Down The Crown more playable by changing its Seasons requirements from Summer, Fall, and Winter to Spring, Summer, and Fall.

Nerfs
• Removed Overkill from The Yearning Woods’ Hanger Tantrum.
• Crows summoned by Prophet of Ruin now fulfill the Self-Fulfilling Prophecy even when they die from being overflowed from the board.
• Increased Radd-Head Trapper’s mana cost from 2 to 3 and increased its Attack from 1 to 2.
• To allow creature-deficient decks to stand a chance, Uncovered Goldcap’s rage requirements for its abilities have been changed to be 1 for Befuddling Spores, 2 for Wind-Up Punch, and 3 for Fungi Flurry.
• To curb the multiplicative increase of infestations from Marrow Maggot, it was changed from a 3/2 that Infests two random abilities when it attacks to a 3/3 that Infests one random ability when it attacks.
• Increased the cooldown on Maestro Maev’s Crescendo ability from 3 to 4 turns in order to encourage more viable strategies against her.
• Increased Burden cost of Bundle of Snakes from 1 to 2 in order to increase the challenge against Borrowed Life deck archetypes.

Reworks
• To increase synergy with the rest of the card pool, Brain Drinker’s passive ability has been changed from “When you reduce my mana cost, do it three times” to “The first time you cast a spell each turn, reduce my cost by 1”.
• In order to form a more cohesive encounter with more of a strategic sense of push and pull, The Shambling City’s Titanic Strike ability has been changed to Excavate, which is a Counterattack that deals 5 and refills its Remaining Residents by the amount overkilled.
• Reworked Tiny Hoof from “When you summon a creature with Frontline, grant it +2 health” to “Grant the first creature you summon each turn +1 health, or +2 health if it has Frontline” to improve its synergy with the rest of the card pool.
• Reworked the Hivemind ability to “Creatures that could have attacked, but did not, deal their damage to the oldest Jellyfish, and take damage equal to its remaining counters.” This change offers more strategic options to the encounter since you can now choose between damaging the Hivemind directly or picking off its Jellyfish friends one by one.
• Reworked Lord Bug from a 5/5 with “Overlord: Summon two Lone Ladybugs” to a 4/4 with “Overlord: Grant myself +1/+1 and summon a Lone Ladybug” and reworked Monarch Butterfly from a 6/6 with “Overlord: Summon two Lord Bugs” to a 5/5 with “Overlord: Grant myself +1/+1 and summon a Lord Bug” with the intent to reduce their tendencies to overcrowd one’s board.

Bug Fixes
• Damage based on the percentage of the enemy’s maximum health now scales correctly against the Prophet of Ruin after the Self-Fulfilling Prophecy is fulfilled.
• Fixed a bug in the Gilded Grifter encounter that would display damage intended as being dealt to creatures when it would really be dealt to the player.
• Grafting a card with a reduced cost no longer resets the card’s cost.
• Death March now generates the correct amount of mana reliably.

Clarity Improvements
• Clarified vocabulary and/or improved wording on Man With The Goat’s Head, Death March, Ferrous Firebomb, Sword Runner, Wave of Lava, and Wildfire Drake.
• Reworded Infest abilities to “bursting infestations” rather than “summoning your infest creatures”.

notes.title: April 1st Patch
notes.notes:
Ravagers have been struggling to rip and tear across the wastelands compared to their feathered Empiricist rivals, who have been hiding behind Borrowed Life in relative safety. This patch reduces the simplicity of forming such protective nests, as well as provides some early survivability to key Ravager units, including the pivotal Vent Crawler passive. You'll also find some clarity and function updates to Infest which are an intended buff to the Sylvans, to make that archetype more self-sufficient. 

Keeper's Rite's have been increased in difficulty, as some players found the hardest challenges available still not a match for their card-flinging prowess. There are some bonus changes too, so read the full notes below if you'd like to be spoiled!

[b]Reworks:[/b]
Infest clarity rework. All cards with Infest can now give a +2 cost Metamorphose.

[b]Card Buffs:[/b]
Impling: 3/1 => 3/2
Vein Drainer: Life cost to summon 2 => 1
Death March: Now also draws a card to give you more fuel to play out!

[b]Card Nerfs:[/b]
Chanting Cultist: 1 Borrowed Life, +1 if you have another Cultist => +1 Borrowed Life flat.
Leviathan: 4 mana => 5 mana
Valdrada: 9/9 => 6/6

[b]Faction Buffs:[/b]
Ravager Vent Crawler: 1/1 => 2/2
Empiricist Healing: 3 per combat => 2 per combat

[b]Keeper's Rites:[/b]
Most of the rites have been made significantly more punishing. Face an even greater challenge!

[b]Major Bug Fixes:[/b]
Fixes a bug with Fearless, Skyscraper Sword and temporary buffs causing bouncing/unusual attack values.
Fixes odd behavior when trying to Double-Cast Swallow on a 1 hp unit.

notes.title: 24 Hours Later: AotA Road Map
notes.notes:
[h2]Acolyte of the Altar has officially been out for 24 hours, and we can't thank you all enough for your support![/h2]

Every review, every piece of feedback, every new discord member has been so cool to see. We want to make sure Acolyte of the Altar is shaped heavily by the hands of our players and community members, so [b]here are the first steps on the road ahead:[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/81f6978a2a58655499ecbfca4fd2ff9158a48dec.png[/img]
Excited to follow this road map as we continue to welcome in new acolytes!

Also, thanks to all of you, we are at the top of Steam's "New and Trending" games!

notes.title: We Launch TOMORROW
notes.notes:
[h2]Hey everyone![/h2]

Three years ago I was pacing the cul-de-sac of an unexceptional suburban town in the southern United States, not far from where uranium was first refined, trying to come up with a name for a company. The name could be in use for quite a long time, so it was a bit like deciding on a tattoo. The one thing I knew for sure was that we wanted to play in the space between games-for-fun and games-for-art. We wanted to shock and ask questions, but also to make something that slipped you into the warm sea of digital dopamine that is video games. So the image of a macabre-toned children’s toy became a mascot for this intrepid little five person team.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/a191652df6a35d486fba637ebeb1e198c3fdacbd.png[/img]

[b]Acolyte of the Altar is our debut creation under this vision.[/b] It’s a game about the nature of needlessly killing things, disguised as a perfectly ordinary card game. One inspired by everything from huddling excitedly and shrimp-backed over our childhood Magic decks, to the competitive ladders of most of  today’s multiplayer CCGs. But also by some of my favorite books, films, and of course other games. It was made possible through tremendous and tireless support of friends and family, as well as the help of content creators and Discord community members who have helped us polish this game from a wonky lump of minerals into quite a smooth and shiny gem. 

If you are reading these words, thank you for finding us! I appreciate each person we run into, because we have exerted great effort to reach out upward into the mist and grab hold of solid stone. In what will forever be one of the most badass stunts toward this end, our social media manager even took to the streets of LA with a cryptic sign reading “SLAY THE BEASTS” and converted random passersby to the cause. Speaking of strangers, this team is unusual in that it was created entirely from people who did not know each other beforehand. So, cheers to whatever stroke of luck allowed us to form such an exceptional group of tip-top talent from the vast untamed jungles of the internet. The team’s dedication and trust that this project would be worth choosing to complete was truly invaluable. Your game is only as strong as the weakest component, and I am lucky to have no idea where to lay that burden.

[b]So, players, thank you for following this journey[/b], or if you are new, welcome and we hope you enjoy summoning some cool creatures and firing off some spells with us. [b]We’ll see you all tomorrow, March 25th[/b]. We’re very excited about Acolyte of the Altar and it’s been an honor to get to create and have fun alongside you.

Cameron Reid
Founder, Black Kite Games

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/1b5e490a8a69d51961710f53a24509140d4565c3.png[/img]

notes.title: Acolyte of the Altar Launches March 25th!
notes.notes:
[h1]It's happening, acolytes.

After three years of work, our debut game as a studio launches on [b]March 25th![/b][/h1]

As a five-person team, it feels surreal that we’re almost finished with development. From starting this studio in 2021, growing a community of people that gave us invaluable feedback, to only having the finishing touches left, this has been a wild journey. We hope all the thought and work put into our game will resonate with players in each encounter through the wastelands. 

To give you another glimpse of what's in store, we’ve highlighted a few more of the game's Beasts: Prophet of Ruin, Forgotten Warrior, Mother of Kid, Noble Guardian, and Sickly Serpentskin. Here, we’ll go through their backstories, offering a closer look at their motivations and traits.

[h2]The Soul of Science[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/d3cc9e26f5ef21ebfba2297cfb984866dd520a79.png[/img]
Lover of Unheeded Messenger, together they tried to warn the world of the dangers that brought the world to waste. As calamities mounted the air turned sour, the land would not sprout crops, sickness rooted itself deeply and the oceans lay barren. The skeptics were never converted by [b]Prophet of Ruin[/b], they simply poisoned themselves away.

[h2]The Soul of the Cosmos[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/98e166862b4fa7e245ecf565a89012ebec64aaa3.png[/img]
Father of the world, disgraced and forgotten. Once their leader in both war and peace, [b]Forgotten Warrior[/b] is now left with a hollow stare that crosses over the horizon and past the orbits of the spheres. Prone to sudden violence, few dare approach for fear of being struck down by bolts of sun and sky.

[h2]The Soul of Love and Family[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/7e2351e3840c78c3641879185768794a2ecad322.png[/img]
A forest spirit once able to shapeshift into any animal, [b]Mother of Kid[/b]'s last supporter is said to have passed away while she was climbing a sheer cliff. She protects her child at all costs. The Kid, who follows close behind, trusts her mother with all her heart.

[h2]The Soul of Bravery[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/0b756e43c13f9fbba2fb8df134f082831a5da715.png[/img]
Aged and ill-equipped to stop outsiders, the [b]Noble Guardian[/b] still holds his post protecting the Sunken Valley. Known for his exceptionally hard shell and indefatigable spirit, the Noble Guardian knows he may not stop any invaders, but he will take ample time to be slain.

[h2]The Soul of Theatre[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/c51e1a3e0e91e1aa2eb4f9e5f80be005a9895185.png[/img]
Brother of Maev. His cup masks, once used in whimsical plays, are now the object of petty street games. A devout of the old ways, [b]Gilded Grifter[/b] helps provide the King of Beggars with food from wandering traders and does his best to unite and entertain what little community is left.

[h3]Alright, that's it for now! Back to work. Thank you again for joining us on this journey, and we'll see you all on [b]March 25th![/b]

- Cameron and the BKG Team[/h3]

notes.title: Slay the Spire meets Hearthstone as new card game sets release date
notes.notes:
Acolyte of the Altar is a roguelike deck builder that, on the digital table, more closely resembles a traditional collectible card game such as Hearthstone or Magic the Gathering than it does the likes of Slay the Spire or Monster Train. Built by Black Kite Games, founded in 2020 by former Red Dead Redemption 2 designer Cameron Reid, and inspired by the grand boss battles of Shadow of the Colossus, the Acolyte of the Altar release date has officially been confirmed, and you can try the game now with a free Steam demo.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: The Bestiary
notes.notes:
[h3]Beasts are at the heart of [i][b]Acolyte of the Altar[/b][/i].[/h3] 
Serving as the game’s enemies, the Beasts are what the player will spend most of their time slaying throughout their journey. These giants vary in appearance and design, with a wide range of abilities and backstories that give them a great degree of depth. But despite opposing the player, these Beasts aren’t inherently evil. They’re living, breathing creatures with deep backgrounds and traits that bring them to life.

To give you a better understanding of how some of these creatures function, we’ve highlighted five of the game’s many Beasts: Hydrozoan Hivemind, The King of Beggars, The Shambling City, The Yearning Woods, and The Unheeded Messenger. Here, we’ll go through their backstories, offering a closer look at their motivations and traits.

[h2]The Soul of Nature[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/81b6082f9cd54e26882fd26f664b6d304dc2e00d.png[/img]
The [b]Hydrozoan Hivemind[/b] was created to explore the concept of spawning additional enemies, just like a classic raid boss would! It's a strange entity that used to haunt the ruddy waters off the coasts of the Red Shores, but it grew sick from the oils released into the ocean by the Ravagers’ industrialization. In an effort to escape pollution, it changed its inner biology and grew lungs, among other mutations. It floated up, by mechanisms unknown, out of the sea, and towards healthier realms, restoring life where its limp tendrils were able. No one has spoken to it, but the Sylvans whisper that pain inflicted on the spawn of the Hive will cause it to flinch, as if they share a single mind.

[h2]The Soul of Humility[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/82a56f0ddd3ce7269f553ffa2cef866e86fcf310.png[/img]
The [b]King of Beggars[/b] was one of the first Beasts we made and one that contains a mystery for players plainly before him: a small bowl of coins, mostly empty. What could have brought such a holy creature to such humble circumstances? In the game, you’ll have to fight against these coins imbued with divine magic as well as a mysterious stranger who occasionally adds a coin when passing by… A long time ago, the King of Beggars was showered with riches by those giving up the material in hope of immaterial gain. Into the cliff-side giant golden vaults were carved, inscribed with his long form winding around their locks. Now the silks that once robed his body are long ruined, and his large form now struggles to find sustenance.

[h2]The Soul of Community[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/c2ab7bb7221387b5638296b90e63749e996fd254.png[/img]
The [b]Shambling City[/b] is a lost capital which helped facilitate trade across the entirety of the wastes by being a mobile hub of commerce. This Beast is one of the few with surviving followers. They will pelt you with rocks from the rooftops and even help convert your creatures to join their ranks! The walking behemoth was built up with Houses worshiping the Forgotten Warrior, the King of Beggars and the City itself. Their true names can still be found inscribed on the cracked and cobwebbed temple walls. 

[h2]The Soul of Nourishment[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/2a9da613f7fbeda3ff855402723a94e45a4ac78b.png[/img]
The [b]Yearning Woods[/b] is an ancient being that now resides in Sylvan territory. It feeds the forest through its fruit and on the forest through its maw. It doesn’t matter to the Beast what you are exactly, only where you are in the cycle of life. The Yearning Woods desires both to nourish the hungry and consume what is ripe! Within the game, it has the unique ability to swallow your creatures whole and can be killed by either overfeeding it to bursting or starving it by only summoning creatures that are too big to digest!

[h2]The Soul of Knowledge[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/3e940ab9dd181578a8df91932d1f616b4b044992.png[/img]
Lover of the Prophet of Ruin, the [b]Unheeded Messenger[/b] is a gentle and caring creature who seeks above all to reduce suffering. She is widely resented for her lofty appearance and is distrusted due to her unfamiliar knowledge. The Unheeded Messenger's great dream was to stop the world from crossing the event horizon of the wasted state it is in today. In game, she sends the player Letters, which warn of different disasters that can impact the encounter. This brings us to another pillar of Acolyte of the Altar’s story: these references of a super-ancient civilization that led the world to becoming the wastelands. Perhaps that civilization distrusted the Messenger as much as the Acolytes today and likewise fell into the hands of Ruin?

[b]That's all for now, acolytes. We will share even more with you all soon!

- Cameron and the BKG Team[/b]

notes.title: Acolyte of the Altar Release Date Announced!

[h3][b]The good news is that we have a more exact release date: March 2024![/b][/h3]
These extra few months will allow us the time to create a perfectly baked game, as well as avoid the holiday season, which will result in more attention at launch and allow us to provide better post-launch support for you all. 

Thank you for understanding and following along in our journey (and baking metaphors.) This is what we love to do and, without you all, we'd have to do something else![/i]

notes.title: Major Demo Update and Bug Hunt Event: Bone Keepers
notes.notes:
[h1]Hello, acolytes! You’re overdue for a big update, and we certainly have one for you.[/h1]

As many of you know, we launched the Acolyte of the Altar demo at [i]Steam Next Fest[/i] back in June, and it was a great success! We gained thousands of wishlists on Steam, and had multiple content creators in the card game world try us out and share us with their audiences. It was an amazing beginning of our home stretch to AotA’s full game release.

Much of the credit to our demo’s success is because of you, acolytes. Everyone who gave feedback on the demo, and all of you who participated in our Bug Hunt event over in the discord provided us with the resources to fine-tune AotA in ways, as a five-person dev team, we would not have been able to otherwise. Thank you for all of your efforts in helping our game be the best it can be!

[h2]Now, for the upcoming news:[/h2] 
In just a couple weeks, we are pushing a [i]major[/i] update to the demo: [b]Keeper’s Rites[/b] mode. Each time you complete a run successfully, you may choose one of the Keeper’s Bones: unique features that will increase the difficulty of your journey. The more rites you complete, the more bones you can activate on your next run. We are excited to see how this brings more replay-ability and customization to the experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43754306/986f6b86dc6cb275dbb6be892e101f321189258f.png[/img]

Because this is a major update to the game, we are asking for your help once more. [b]From August 21st-August 27th[/b], get ready to participate in [b]Bug Hunt: Bone Keepers Edition.[/b] Join the Acolyte of the Altar Discord [url=https://discord.gg/7sRDf9tdxN]here[/url] to be notified when the demo goes live and connect with your fellow acolytes as we all submit bug reports, give suggestions, and prepare for our next big Steam press event!

*To peel back the curtain a bit, Steam wishlists are key to the success of indie game releases, and with 2.3k currently, we need to keep momentum to reach our goal of at least 7k. We’re confident that announcing this new demo update will give us the push we need to grow our wishlist count before launch!

[h2]Acolyte of the Altar is [i]mere months away[/i] from release, and we are so thankful for all of you joining us on the journey. Let’s hunt some bugs![/h2]

- Cameron and the BKG Team
